bib.title: M3-Embedding: Multi-Linguality, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings Through Self-Knowledge Distillation
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024, pages 2318-2335

question: Can one embedding model support 100+ languages, dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval, and inputs up to 8192 tokens, and does combining the three scores help?
hypothesis: Relevance scores from heterogeneous retrieval functions can be integrated as a teacher signal so the functions reinforce rather than conflict, and hybrid scoring beats each alone.
contributions: M3-Embedding with unified multi-linguality, multi-functionality, multi-granularity
Self-knowledge distillation training framework and efficient batching, plus data curation
Model, code and data publicly released

method.summary: XLM-RoBERTa-large extended to 8192 positions and adapted with RetroMAE, then contrastively pre-trained on 1.2B multilingual pairs (dense only) and fine-tuned with self-knowledge distillation where the weighted sum of dense, lexical and multi-vector scores teaches each head. Hybrid retrieval re-ranks with a weighted sum of the three scores.
method.task: multilingual, cross-lingual and long-document retrieval with a single embedding model

datasets.name: Unsupervised pre-training data
datasets.source: MTP 291.1M (EN,ZH); S2ORC+Wikipedia 48.3M (EN); xP3, mC4, CC-News 488.4M (multilingual); NLLB, CCMatrix 391.3M (cross-lingual); CodeSearchNet 344.1K
datasets.preprocessing: filtered for bad content and low relevance; for long texts, with probability 0.2% a passage is split into three segments and shuffled

datasets.name: Labeled fine-tuning data
datasets.source: EN: HotpotQA, TriviaQA, NQ, MS MARCO, COLIEE, PubMedQA, SQuAD, SimCSE NLI; ZH: DuReader, mMARCO-ZH, T2-Ranking, LawGPT, CMedQAv2, NLI-zh, LeCaRDv2

datasets.name: MultiLongDoc (synthetic)
datasets.size: 41.4K train; Table 7: 41,434 train, 2,600 dev, 3,800 test, 493,709 corpus docs, 13 languages
datasets.source: Wikipedia, Wudao, mC4 articles; GPT-3.5 generates one question per sampled paragraph; question paired with the full article

datasets.name: MKQA
datasets.size: 25 non-English query languages vs English Wikipedia (BEIR NQ corpus)

models.name: M3-Embedding
models.architecture: XLM-RoBERTa-large encoder, max position extended to 8192; CLS embedding for dense, ReLU(W_lex h) per-token weight for sparse, projection W_mul for ColBERT-style multi-vector

models.name: mDPR, mContriever, mE5-large, E5-mistral-7b, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, ada-002, jina-embeddings-v2-base-en

training.objective: InfoNCE per retrieval function plus self-knowledge distillation: L_final=(L+L')/2, with teacher s_inter=w1*s_dense+w2*s_lex+w3*s_mul and L'=-p(s_inter)*log p(s_*); L=(l1 Ldense+l2 Llex+l3 Lmul+Linter)/4
training.lr: RetroMAE stage 7e-5; unsupervised stage 5e-5; fine-tune lr not stated
training.warmup: unsupervised stage warmup ratio 0.1; fine-tune: about 6000 warm-up steps training dense/sparse/multi-vector before unified SKD training
training.batch_size: RetroMAE batch 32 with gradient accumulation 16; unsupervised and fine-tune total batch sizes vary by length from 67,200 to 9,984 and 1,152 to 192 (Table 9)
training.hardware: RetroMAE 32 A100 40GB; unsupervised 96 A800 80GB; fine-tune 24 A800 80GB

other.retromae_data: 184M samples from Pile, Wudao, mC4, 105 languages
other.efficient_batching: group by length, split-batch with gradient checkpointing, cross-GPU embedding broadcast; batch size per device at length 8192 rises 6 -> 130 (Table 10)
other.MCLS: insert a [CLS] every 256 tokens at inference and average last hidden states; no training

inference.samples: single run; no seeds or significance test stated
inference.retrieval: Dense: Faiss top-1000. Sparse: Lucene index top-1000. Multi-vec: rerank top-200 of dense. Dense+Sparse: rerank union of top-1000 each. All: rerank top-200 of dense.

metrics.name: Recall@100
metrics.definition: primary for MKQA; Recall@20 in appendix

eval.protocol: Single reported run per cell; BM25 uses the XLM-R tokenizer for comparability; no significance tests stated.

results.claim: On MIRACL dev, all three retrieval functions combined give the best average nDCG@10.

results.note: baseline is BM25 with XLM-R tokenizer; 38.5 with Lucene analyzer (Table 11)

results.claim: M3 dense alone beats mE5-large on MIRACL average.
M3 sparse alone beats BM25 on MIRACL average (same XLM-R tokenizer) but is far below dense.
Dense+Sparse hybrid improves over dense alone on MIRACL.
Multi-vector reranking of dense top-200 beats dense on MIRACL.
On MKQA cross-lingual retrieval, All gives the best Recall@100.
results.setup: MKQA, 25 query languages vs English Wikipedia

results.claim: On MKQA, M3 sparse is poor because query and passage share few terms across languages.
On long documents (MLDR) sparse beats dense by about 10 points.
results.setup: MLDR test, 13 languages, 8192 tokens, M3 Sparse
results.quote: which achieves another about 10 points improvement over the dense method

results.note: baseline is BM25 with XLM-R tokenizer, max length 8192; Dense+Sparse is 64.8

results.claim: On NarrativeQA, All is best and beats E5-mistral-7b and text-embedding-3-large.
Removing self-knowledge distillation collapses the sparse head on MIRACL.
results.setup: MIRACL dev, M3 sparse trained without skd
results.note: baseline is with skd; dense 68.7 vs 69.2, multi-vec 69.3 vs 70.5

results.setup: MIRACL dev, Dense: fine-tune only 60.5; RetroMAE+fine-tune 66.1; RetroMAE+Unsup+fine-tune 69.2

results.setup: MLDR test, Dense-w.o.long with MCLS vs without
results.quote: MCLS can significantly improve the performance of document retrieval without training (41.2 → 45.0)

results.claim: Split-batch lets the per-device batch size grow by over 20x at length 8192.
Lucene analyzer yields 37% more unique terms per MLDR article than the XLM-R tokenizer, raising latency.

the tokenizer of XLM-RoBERTa produces 1056 unique terms per article, while Lucene’s analyzer gen-

limits: Authors concede generalisation beyond MIRACL/MKQA to other datasets and real-world scenarios is untested.
Performance on documents over 8192 tokens or extremely long documents is not studied.
Per-language variation across the claimed 100+ languages is not thoroughly analysed.
Fusion weights w1..w3 are hand-set per benchmark (different for MLDR vs MIRACL), no tuning procedure given.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; parameter count, fine-tune lr, tau and optimizer not stated.
Hybrid All uses only top-200 dense candidates; recall of the pipeline is bounded by the dense first stage.
BM25 baseline in main tables uses XLM-R tokenizer; with Lucene analyzer BM25 is stronger (MLDR 64.1 vs M3 sparse 62.2).
Hybrid here fuses learned scores from one model, not independent BM25 and dense systems.

terms.definition: insert multiple CLS tokens (one per 256 tokens) into a long document at inference and average their embeddings
the integrated relevance score from dense, lexical and multi-vector functions is used as teacher for each function
